tasks.short: Plan training sessions around rooms, forklifts, instructors and shift rosters on three sites, then send invites.

today.trigger: A certificate (forklift, VCA, food safety) is close to expiry, a new group of hires or flex workers starts, or a manager asks for a course.
steps: Pull expiring certificates and open enrolments from Studytube into Excel
Check shift rosters in AFAS and ask team leads who can be released
Check room calendars and forklift or training-equipment availability per site by mail and Teams
Agree dates with the external instructor or training provider
Book in Studytube, send Outlook invites, and rebook when people swap shifts or call in sick
drudgery: Copying names between Studytube, AFAS and Excel
Chasing team leads for release from shifts
Rebooking after shift swaps, absence and no-shows
today.time_sinks: Matching three calendars (shift roster, room or equipment, instructor) by hand and redoing it when one changes; flex workers from agencies are not in AFAS rosters.

lenses.faster: A scheduler reads expiry dates from Studytube and rosters from AFAS and proposes filled sessions per site; the copy-paste and calendar matching steps disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Each night a job finds certificates expiring within 60 days, books the person on a session on a day they are rostered, and sends invites to employee and team lead.
lenses.ambitious: Nobody works a shift with a lapsed forklift or VCA certificate, and every new hire, including agency staff, is booked on mandatory training before the first shift.
lenses.joy: No more chasing team leads and redoing schedules after every shift swap; the specialist keeps the conversations with instructors and site leads.
lenses.options: The scheduler offers two or three session plans per site (fewer, fuller sessions against faster certification) with the cost and lapse risk of each.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the scheduling rules (lead times, group sizes, release limits per shift, which certificates block which tasks) and reviews the weekly exception list.
reach: HR Administrator: keeping certificate data in AFAS and Studytube in sync
Site and shift planners: release planning for training
Recruiter: booking mandatory training as part of the offer-to-first-shift flow

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating release with site leads in peak season and judging when a lapse can be covered by reassigning tasks instead of pulling someone off a shift.
tasks.pattern_why: Inputs are structured (expiry dates, rosters, room and instructor calendars) and the rules can be written down; the output is a checkable booking, so no model is needed at run time.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly run after the AFAS extract refresh, plus new-hire and agency-start events.
steps: Read certificate expiry dates and enrolments from Studytube and rosters from AFAS
Read room and equipment calendars in Outlook and instructor availability
Fill sessions by rules: rostered day, site, group size, release limit per shift
Book in Studytube and send Outlook invites to employee and team lead
Put conflicts, agency staff without rosters and unfillable sessions on an exception list
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the exception list and any session that pulls more people off a shift than the release limit.
data_needed: Certificate types, expiry dates and which tasks they block
Agency worker start dates and planned shifts
in_practice.logs_to: A scheduling log in SharePoint with every booking, rebooking and override, plus the Studytube enrolment history.

evidence.claim: Studytube holds courses, enrolments and mandatory certificates with expiry dates that a scheduler can read.
Certificate expiry, enrolment and scheduling fit deterministic software at autonomy 4, booking shift staff from Studytube expiry dates and AFAS rosters before a lapse.
Constraint-based scheduling of sessions against rosters and room calendars is routine software.

risks: Rosters in AFAS may lag real shift swaps, causing no-shows
Agency flex workers are outside AFAS rosters, so the riskiest group is the least covered
Automated booking off shifts can clash with CAO rest and working-time rules if not encoded
A tool that tracks attendance per person may count as monitoring-capable and need works council consent (WOR 27(1)(l))
research_questions: How many certificates lapsed, or nearly lapsed, in the last 12 months and on which sites?
Do Studytube and AFAS expose APIs or exports good enough for a nightly job, including agency staff?
How many hours a month do the two specialists spend on booking and rebooking today?
Does the works council see an automated attendance and booking tool as needing consent?

tasks.short: Track what we spend on training per site and department, and write budget reports explaining it.

today.trigger: Month close, the quarterly budget review with the HR Director and Finance, or a question about why training cost went up.
steps: Export training invoices and cost lines from AFAS accounts payable and the general ledger
Match provider invoices to Studytube courses and participants in Excel
Add agency invoices for training hours of flex workers
Split cost per site, department and course type (mandatory against development)
Write a short explanation of variances against budget for HR and Finance
drudgery: Matching invoices to courses and people by hand
Rebuilding the same Excel each quarter
today.time_sinks: Invoices that do not name the course or participants, and training hours hidden in agency invoices.

lenses.faster: A Power BI page on the nightly AFAS extract joins invoices, Studytube enrolments and cost centres; the monthly matching in Excel disappears.
lenses.autonomous: At month close the report refreshes itself and a model drafts the variance note from the numbers; unmatched invoices go to the bookkeeper as a list.
lenses.ambitious: Cost per certified shift worker and cost per productive hire become visible per site, so L&D can show what training adds to 90-day retention instead of only what it costs.
lenses.joy: No more rebuilding the quarterly Excel; what is left is explaining choices to the HR Director and Finance.
lenses.options: Three budget scenarios for next year (peak-season flex intake high, medium, low) with mandatory certificate cost driven by headcount.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the cost model and the coding rules for training costs and checks the drafted note before it goes out.
reach: FP&A Analyst: training line in the HR budget and forecast
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: linking training cost to retention

tasks.human_edge: Arguing why a programme is worth its cost to the HR Director, Finance and the works council, and deciding what to cut when the budget is tight.
tasks.pattern_why: Cost lines, invoices and enrolments are structured and the joins and splits can be written as rules; a small llm step only drafts the variance note, checked against the numbers.

in_practice.trigger: Month close in AFAS and the nightly Power BI refresh.
steps: Join AFAS general ledger and accounts payable lines on training cost codes with Studytube enrolments
Add training hours from agency invoices by code
Show cost per site, department, course type and certified worker against budget
Draft a variance note from the figures with an llm step, citing each number
List unmatched or miscoded invoices for the bookkeeper
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist checks and signs the variance note before it goes to the HR Director and Finance.
data_needed: Training cost codes and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset history and the monthly report archive in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Power BI HR and finance dashboards already run on a nightly AFAS extract at Noordhaven.
Cost reports for training fit deterministic software at autonomy 4.
A language model can draft a variance narrative from a table of figures.

risks: Inconsistent cost coding in AFAS makes the dashboard wrong but credible
A drafted note can misstate a cause the numbers do not show
Per-person cost views can drift into individual monitoring; keep reports at group level
research_questions: What share of training invoices today can be matched to a course and site without manual work?
Are training hours in agency invoices coded separately or bundled with regular hours?
Does Finance accept a model-drafted variance note if every number links to the source?

tasks.short: Design programmes that grow shift leads and office staff into future managers.

today.trigger: Annual talent review, a hard-to-fill team lead or site manager vacancy, or a request from the HR Director or a site manager.
steps: Talk with HR Business Partners and site managers about who has potential and which roles will open
Look for programme formats, providers and internal mentors
Design the programme: modules, assignments, mentoring, selection
Get budget and approval from the HR Director and inform the works council
Run intake and follow participants over the year
drudgery: Collecting succession and vacancy data from several people
Writing programme descriptions and invitations from scratch
today.time_sinks: Many conversations to agree who is in scope, and building materials and business cases each year.

lenses.faster: A copilot drafts programme outlines, provider comparisons, briefing notes for HR Business Partners and the business case from the specialist's notes; the specialist edits.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone: at most a quarterly summary of team lead and manager vacancies from Recruitee and AFAS that prompts the talent review.
lenses.ambitious: A real internal route from forklift driver or planner to team lead and site manager on all three sites, so more lead roles are filled internally and those people stay.
lenses.joy: Less time writing decks and comparing brochures; more time with participants, mentors and site managers.
lenses.options: Four programme designs (in-house cohort, provider programme, mentoring plus stretch assignments, blended) with cost, time off shift and expected internal fill rate.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the internal leadership pipeline as a system: entry criteria, open nomination, measures agreed with managers up front and checked at six weeks and six months.
reach: HR Business Partner: succession planning input
Recruiter: internal candidates for team lead vacancies
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: internal fill and retention measures

tasks.human_edge: Spotting and encouraging people who would not put themselves forward, fair selection, and the trust of site managers and participants.
tasks.pattern_why: The work is judgement and relationships with people; AI helps with research, drafts and options, but selection and development decisions stay with HR.

in_practice.trigger: Annual talent review or a manager request for a development programme.
steps: Specialist gives the copilot the goals, budget, target group and constraints (shifts, CAO)
Copilot drafts programme options, provider comparison and business case
Specialist tests the options with HR Business Partners and site managers
Copilot drafts participant materials and briefings; specialist edits
Measures are agreed with managers before start and reviewed at six weeks and six months
in_practice.human_gate: HR Director and the specialist decide the programme and who takes part; AI does not rank or select people.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or a similar assistant
in_practice.logs_to: Programme file in SharePoint with design decisions, approvals and measures.

evidence.claim: Learning teams use AI to draft content with a person reviewing, and agree measures with managers before collecting them at six weeks and six months.
evidence.source: HRD Connect with MHR, digest S4

evidence.claim: Microsoft's learning agent shows skill gaps, pathways and mentors while HR still guides role moves and leadership development.
Practice with an AI feedback coach improved the quality of managers' feedback write-ups.
evidence.source: Workday with Sana, digest S2 (vendor on itself)

risks: Using AI to score or rank 'potential' would be high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III 4(b) from 2 December 2027 and needs works council consent
Bias against shift workers, part-timers or flex workers who are less visible in data
Generic AI-drafted programmes that do not fit warehouse and transport reality
research_questions: How many team lead and site manager roles were filled internally in the last two years, and did they stay?
Do shift staff want a leadership route, and what stops them (hours, language, shifts)?
What does the works council expect in consultation on a development programme under WOR 27(1)(f)?

tasks.short: Build training on fuel-saving driving, waste separation and energy use in warehouses and offices.

today.trigger: A sustainability target from management, a customer audit or tender question, Code 95 refresher needs, or new waste rules.
steps: Gather input from fleet, facility and site managers on what goes wrong
Find or write content (eco-driving, foil and pallet recycling, energy use)
Build a Studytube module or a toolbox talk for team leads
Plan delivery around shifts and track completion
Report participation for audits or customer questions
drudgery: Writing course text and quiz questions from scratch
Making Dutch and other language versions for flex workers
Collecting completion figures for audit questions
today.time_sinks: Content creation and translation for a mixed-language workforce on a topic that comes up only a few times a year.

lenses.faster: Studytube AI Authoring drafts the module, quiz and a toolbox-talk script from site procedures and supplier documents; the specialist and a site expert review instead of writing.
lenses.autonomous: Completion reports for audits and tenders refresh from Studytube on request; new hires are enrolled automatically in the short waste-separation module.
lenses.ambitious: Short site-specific modules in the languages flex workers speak, tied to measured fuel use per route and waste per site, instead of one generic course every few years.
lenses.joy: No more writing quiz questions and translations by hand; the specialist keeps the site walks and talks with drivers and team leads.
lenses.options: Several formats from the same source: five-minute toolbox talk, e-learning, poster, and a driver tip sheet, with the choice made per site.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns a small library of approved source material and review steps, and checks whether fuel and waste figures move after training.
reach: Facility and fleet managers: content on waste and fuel
Controller or FP&A: linking training to fuel and waste cost
Sustainability reporting: training evidence for customer and tender questions

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what drivers and warehouse staff actually do on the floor, getting site experts to sign off, and making the message credible to shift workers.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured source documents become a structured course, quiz and translations inside the Studytube workflow, with a person approving before release.

in_practice.trigger: A request from fleet or facility management, an audit question, or a new rule.
steps: Specialist uploads site procedures and source documents to Studytube AI Authoring
AI drafts outline, module text, quiz and toolbox-talk script, plus language versions
Site or fleet expert checks facts; specialist edits for reading level
Publish in Studytube and enrol target groups by rule
Compare completion with fuel and waste figures per site after three and six months
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist and a site or fleet expert approve content before publishing; Code 95 hours run only through a recognised provider.
data_needed: Fuel and waste figures per site
Language profile of the target group
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube course version history and the review sign-off in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts outlines, scripts and questions from a title or uploaded PDF, PPT or SCORM; authors edit.
Faster content is the main way L&D teams use AI today.
No opened source shows AI-made courses cutting time-to-skill, so the effect on fuel or waste must be measured here.

risks: Wrong or generic facts in drafted content if site experts do not check
Machine translations that shift workers find unclear
Training counted as done without any change in fuel or waste
research_questions: Which sites have measurable fuel and waste data that could show an effect?
Which languages do flex workers need, and how good are Studytube's language versions for them?
Would customers or tenders accept Studytube completion reports as evidence?

role.altitude: From producing courses and booking sessions to owning the competence record for 1,200 staff: certificate validity per shift, the scheduling and cost rules, the approved content library, and the AI Act Article 4 measures file.
reach: HR Administrator: certificate and training data in AFAS and Studytube
Site and shift planners: release planning for training
Recruiter: mandatory training booked between offer and first shift
FP&A Analyst: training budget and forecast
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: linking training to onboarding in week one and 90-day retention
HR Business Partner: succession and development planning input
role.ceiling_note: Scheduling and cost reporting can shrink by two thirds (about 90 of 135 hours per FTE a year on these two tasks). Development programmes and practical safety training stay with people; VCA, forklift and Code 95 skills are certified by outside bodies, works council consent is needed for training policy and monitoring-capable tools, and from December 2027 any AI evaluating workers on learning data is high-risk.
skills_to_grow: Writing scheduling and booking rules precisely enough to build and test
Power BI and data joins across AFAS and Studytube
Reviewing AI-drafted content for accuracy and reading level
Agreeing measures with managers before launch and evaluating at six weeks and six months
EU AI Act Article 4 literacy measures and Annex III obligations, plus works council consultation
role.ambitious_version: Every shift worker, including agency staff, is certified before the first shift and never works with a lapsed certificate; onboarding is completed in week one on all three sites; and L&D can show per site how training links to 90-day retention, with a documented AI literacy programme for all 1,200 staff that the works council has agreed to.
